extraction.name: WebWalkerQA
extraction.description: A bilingual benchmark for evaluating LLM web traversal abilities in complex, multi-step information-seeking tasks using question-answer pairs collected from official websites across conference, organization, education, and game domains.
extraction.creator: Jialong Wu, Wenbiao Yin, Yong Jiang, Zhenglin Wang, Zekun Xi, Runnan Fang, Linhai Zhang, Yulan He, Deyu Zhou, Pengjun Xie, Fei Huang
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was built by collecting root official websites in four domains, recursively traversing accessible sub-links and subpages, generating synthetic QA pairs with GPT-4o using predefined rules, and then manually verifying, rewriting, calibrating, filtering, and quality-controlling the QA pairs with human annotators.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Root official websites and their accessible sub-links and subpages from conference, organization, education, and game domains; observations use webpage markdown content and clickable HTML buttons with associated URLs.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Synthetic queries were verified and filtered to remove illegitimate or unnatural questions, retaining only QA pairs with short answers containing entities; human annotators also rewrote and calibrated questions and answers for correctness and consistency.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Official websites were recursively traversed to collect accessible sub-links and pages; page information was used to construct single-source and multi-source queries; webpage markdown content and clickable HTML buttons with URLs were extracted using Beautiful Soup.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: A two-stage funnel annotation strategy combined LLM-based and human annotation: GPT-4o performed initial annotations and synthetic QA generation, then crowd-sourced human annotators conducted quality control, filtering, rewriting, and calibration to refine final QA pairs.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: GPT-4o was used for initial annotations; crowd-sourced human annotators then conducted quality control, filtering, and rewriting/calibration of questions and answers.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The annotation process used human quality control and filtering to refine LLM-generated annotations and manual verification to ensure QA accuracy and relevance.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The work aims to improve scalable and reliable LLM-based information retrieval integrated with RAG through deeper vertical exploration of authoritative web sources.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is limited to official websites in four selected domains and two languages, chosen because they provide authoritative information and rich clickable content.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark is restricted to official websites, four domains, two languages, and click-only actions, and it emphasizes short-answer entity-based QA; evaluation also avoids exact match because generated text lengths vary.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluating LLMs and agent frameworks on web traversal, information-seeking QA, and RAG systems, including performance and efficiency assessment.

name.evidence: To address it, we introduce WebWalkerQA, a benchmark designed to assess the ability of LLMs to perform web traversal.

description.evidence: We propose WebWalkerQA, designed specifically to evaluate LLMs on their ability to handle queries embedded in complex, multi-step web interactions on a given root website. WebWalkerQA focuses on text-based reasoning abilities, using a Question-Answer format to evaluate traversal and problem-solving capabilities in web scenarios.

creator.evidence: Jialong Wu, Wenbiao Yin, Yong Jiang, Zhenglin Wang, Zekun Xi, Runnan Fang, Linhai Zhang, Yulan He, Deyu Zhou, Pengjun Xie, Fei Huang

inLanguage.evidence: WebWalkerQA is a bilingual dataset that includes both Chinese and English

isLiveDataset.evidence: We construct a challenging benchmark, WebWalkerQA, which is composed of 680 queries from four real-world scenarios across over 1373 webpages.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: We first collect root official websites across conference, organization, education, and game domains. Then we mimic human behavior by systematically clicking and collecting subpages accessible through sublinks on the root page. Using predefined rules, we leverage GPT4o to generate synthetic QA-pairs based on the gathered information, followed by manual verification to ensure accuracy and relevance.
